  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Zero-shot Interactive Perception</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Venkatesh Sripada
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>University of Surrey
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">v.sripada@surrey.ac.uk</span></a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Frank Guerin
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>University of Surrey
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">f.guerin@surrey.ac.uk</span></a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Amir Ghalamzan
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>University of Sheffield
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">a.ghalamzan@sheffield.ac.uk</span></a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Interactive perception (IP) enables robots to extract hidden information in their workspace and execute manipulation plans by physically interacting with objects and altering the state of the environment—crucial for resolving occlusions and ambiguity in complex, partially observable scenarios. We present <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Zero-Shot IP (ZS-IP)</span>, a novel framework that couples multi-strategy manipulation (pushing and grasping) with a memory-driven Vision Language Model (VLM) to guide robotic interactions and resolve semantic queries. ZS-IP integrates three key components: (1) an Enhanced Observation (EO) module that augments the VLM’s visual perception with both conventional keypoints and our proposed <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">pushlines</span> —a novel 2D visual augmentation tailored to pushing actions, (2) a memory-guided action module that reinforces semantic reasoning through context lookup, and (3) a robotic controller that executes pushing, pulling, or grasping based on VLM output. Unlike grid-based augmentations optimized for pick-and-place, pushlines capture affordances for contact-rich actions, substantially improving pushing performance. We evaluate ZS-IP on a 7-DOF Franka Panda arm across diverse scenes with varying occlusions and task complexities. Our experiments demonstrate that ZS-IP outperforms passive and viewpoint-based perception techniques such as Mark-Based Visual Prompting (MOKA), particularly in pushing tasks, while preserving the integrity of non-target elements.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para">
<table id="p1.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_top">

<tr id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_tr">

<div id="p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<blockquote id="p2.1" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="p2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Keywords:</span> Robotic manipulation, Perception, Planning</p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Robots are increasingly being deployed in semi-structured environments, dealing with a wide array of unplanned objects and configurations. For example, picking varied items in an e-commerce warehouse, packing boxes, and processing customer returns may involve searching for specific information. A critical challenge in robotic perception arises when robots operate in cluttered or partially observable environments, where objects may be occluded or entirely hidden from view <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>. Traditional approaches, such as active perception <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, address this issue by dynamically adjusting the robot’s viewpoint to gather additional information. However, sometimes it is necessary to move obstacles out of the way, and this is called interactive perception <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite></p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent studies have integrated the manipulation capability with high-level reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> but are limited to performing only pick-and-place or grasping operations.
Also, they remain constrained to static-scene tasks (e.g., “Insert the perfume into the gift box” or “Unplug the cable”) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>. Such approaches cannot accommodate queries that depend on temporal context. For instance, “What is under the eraser?” requires the system to track the eraser’s original location before and after manipulation to terminate the search.
Conventional methods are also limited in terms of generalisation to unseen objects <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>. The ability to interpret natural language queries, reason about object relationships, and plan physical interactions in a cohesive framework is still underdeveloped.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We present ZS-IP, a Zero-Shot Interactive Perception framework that addresses these shortcomings by tightly integrating vision-language models, enhanced visual affordances, and memory-driven action planning. Our key contributions are:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zero-shot Interactive Perception:</span> A novel architecture using a vision-language model to interpret natural-language queries, reason about object relationships, and guide multi-strategy manipulations</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pushlines <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\&amp;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&amp;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\&amp;</annotation></semantics></math> Enhanced Observation</span>: Introduction of pushlines, a 2D visual augmentation that identifies feasible push or pull trajectories, alongside a multi-resolution 2D grid and grasp keypoints (Fig <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), enabling a rich set of physical interactions and dynamic camera re-positioning.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Memory-Guided Action Module</span>: A retrieval-based mechanism that summarizes temporal information across sequential states, ensuring precise, context-aware action selection and termination.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comprehensive Evaluation</span>: Deployment of ZS-IP on a 7-DOF Franka Panda arm across eight interactive perception tasks with varied occlusion and complexity. We demonstrate that ZS-IP significantly outperforms passive and viewpoint-based baselines.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related works</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> and vision-language models (VLMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> have significantly improved high-level reasoning in robotics. However, spatial reasoning remains a core limitation for VLMs  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, largely due to insufficient training data involving object relationships and interactions. Efforts like NEWTON <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, PROST <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, and PIQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> address this gap by exploring physical attributes and affordance reasoning, while SayCan <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, Code as Policies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, and Tidybot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite> integrate LLMs with robotic control through action grounding and in-context learning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Despite these strides, many of these methods struggle in dynamic or partially observable environments where physical interaction is essential. Active perception techniques <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite> enhance scene understanding by changing viewpoints, but rely on static, pre-collected observations, limiting adaptability. Though models like Neural Graspness Fields <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite> reduce uncertainty through next-best-view planning, they do not change the environment to access hidden information.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Interactive perception addresses this limitation by enabling robots to alter the environment directly through actions like pushing or lifting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>. Prior works such as MOKA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> and PIVOT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite> have leveraged visual prompting and 2D spatial annotations to support such tasks. However, these approaches rely on discrete annotations and struggle in cluttered scenes. In contrast, our proposed method uses a continuous 2D grid for more expressive physical reasoning, enhancing success rates in complex, real-world queries.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">While recent frameworks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> have introduced dynamic interaction strategies, they often lack semantic integration, limiting their applicability to predefined object categories. Our work bridges this gap by combining interactive perception with high-level semantic reasoning for generalizable, goal-directed robotic manipulation in unstructured environments.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18374v1/Figures/rss25/InterPer2.png" id="S2.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/253;" width="476" height="253" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span><span id="S2.F1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Zero-shot Interactive Perception Framework:</span> The Perception Analyser (i.e. <math id="S2.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)</annotation></semantics></math>) evaluates the scene observation <math id="S2.F1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> at robot configuration <math id="S2.F1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and attempts to resolve the query, <math id="S2.F1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. If unsuccessful, EO annotates the image, <math id="S2.F1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{o}_{t}=EO(o_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{o}_{t}=EO(o_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, after segmenting target objects with Grounded SAM, e.g. push lines (<math id="S2.F1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{\text{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mtext>P</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{\text{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>), keypoints (<math id="S2.F1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{\text{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mtext>G</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{\text{G}}</annotation></semantics></math>), and 2D grid (<math id="S2.F1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{\text{AP}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mtext>AP</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{\text{AP}}</annotation></semantics></math>). A history of interactions is kept in memory <math id="S2.F1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to avoid redundant actions and enhance task efficiency. Action <math id="S2.F1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is generated to make a proper physical interaction to answer the query. <math id="S2.F1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> states, <math id="S2.F1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> contains both images <math id="S2.F1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and a summary of scene description, <math id="S2.F1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, relevant to query. The robot performs the interaction and saves the corresponding image and robot’s state in <math id="S2.F1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> which then goes to the Perception Analyser. </figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The challenge of integrating semantic reasoning with physical interaction remains a critical bottleneck in robotic perception, affecting applications ranging from inventory assessment of returned packages to delicate object handling, such as clustered strawberry picking. While LLMs and VLMs excel at high-level semantic reasoning, their ability to guide low-level physical interactions remains limited. Efforts like SpatialVLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> have sought to enhance spatial representations, but they primarily rely on static annotations and lack the capability to interact dynamically with their environment. Similarly, physics-based commonsense reasoning frameworks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite> focus on object properties and interactions but do not fully leverage interactive perception to iteratively manipulate and reveal occluded information.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Methodology</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our system, comprising a robotic manipulator equipped with an in-hand camera (Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), acts as an <span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">agent</span> that interacts with its environment to reveal hidden or occluded objects and answer specific queries. The core task involves analysing the scene, performing physical interactions to change the workspace’s state, and iteratively gathering visual data until the VLM can provide a conclusive answer to a query, e.g. ‘<em id="S3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">What is under the eraser?</em>’ in Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> bottom row.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given a natural language query, <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, and an initial visual observation <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math> at time <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the agent uses a <span id="S3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Perception Analyser</span> to output an answer <math id="S3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)</annotation></semantics></math> (see schematic of ZS-IP in Fig. <a href="#S2.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 2 Related works ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). If the answer is not conclusive, ZS-IP generates an action <math id="S3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> to change the scene configuration aiming to maximise the likelihood of answering the query in the next iteration. This is detailed below:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Input Block:</span> It contains the initial visual data from the camera-in-hand image <math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t},t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t},t=0</annotation></semantics></math> (see Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), taken at the robot’s home configuration, <math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the natural language query (e.g., ‘What is under the eraser?’) <math id="S3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. This provides the system with the starting conditions for exploration.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Perception Analyser (PA)</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It interprets visual data and assesses whether the current observation is sufficient to answer the query, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> includes the evaluation of the scene for objects relevant to <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, spatial relationships, and context, and a binary decision: either the query is resolved, or further workspace interaction is required.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Enhanced Observation:</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce the Enhanced Observation (EO), <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{o}</annotation></semantics></math>, which may include the image with overlaid 2-D grid, pushing lines or grasping key points, see Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, top. A segmentation mask, generated using Grounded SAM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>, is used to segment the target object based on a text string descriptor passed by the Perception Analyser (VLM). The mask is provided as input to generate push lines or keypoints
This enhances the VLM to convey its predictive outputs to the robot in the form of planned motions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Push lines <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{P}</annotation></semantics></math>:</em> The agent uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> and computes Principal axis 1 and 2 based on the object segmentation mask
Two principal push lines are generated along the axes passing through the centre of the object segmentation mask and oriented perpendicular to the object’s shape (Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> top right). Additionally, four more push lines are created using key points near the edges of the object’s segmentation mask. These push lines are annotated as <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">P</span> (pre-contact points) and <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">D</span> (post-contact points), followed by indices (e.g., <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">P1-P6</span> and <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">D1-D6</span>). These points define the start and end locations of a virtual push trajectory.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Grasping key points <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{G}</annotation></semantics></math>:</em> We define key points as a set of five points, with four points marking the object boundary (from the segmentation mask) and the fifth being the centroid. The key points are generated using Farthest Point Sampling (fps) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. The key points are overlaid on the image of the segmented target object (Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> bottom raw) with indices <span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">P</span>, i.e. <span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">P1-P5</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Virtual Grid <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{ap}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{ap}</annotation></semantics></math></em>: a 2-D virtual grid is built in the robot workspace and projected into the image frame using an ArUco marker <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> anchoring the grid. Its vertices <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{M}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>M</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V^{M}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined in the camera coordinate frame <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>.
The transformation of these vertices into the robot’s base frame <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is computed using a homogeneous transformation matrix <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{v}^{B}=T_{C}^{B}T_{M_{id}}^{C}V_{v}^{M_{id}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{v}^{B}=T_{C}^{B}T_{M_{id}}^{C}V_{v}^{M_{id}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{M_{id}}^{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{M_{id}}^{C}</annotation></semantics></math> is derived from the camera’s intrinsic parameters using translation and rotation vectors, while <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{C}^{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>B</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{C}^{B}</annotation></semantics></math> is calculated through the robot’s inverse kinematics.
The system continuously updates the translation and rotation vectors as the robot moves, maintaining a consistent grid projection. The agent internally generates a fine grid and zooms where precise coordinates for the robot’s movements are required.
The distance from the camera to the objects is calculated using data from the depth camera. The geometric centre of the segmentation mask is identified, and the depth information corresponding to this point is retrieved and used where needed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Memory-guided action module</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">It consists of robot state representations and memory block that are provided as input to a VLM. The VLM generates an action policy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">State Representation:</span>
The experiment’s state at time <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> captures current configuration of the robot, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the workspaces’ state, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e. summary information of the scene after each interaction, as well as the VLM chain of thought at that time, the states visited, robot trajectory at time <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and the context and knowledge, such as task requirements, constraints and goals.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Memory Block:</span>
Information gathered during each movement is stored and used iteratively to refine subsequent actions, ensuring that the robot accumulates relevant knowledge for query resolution. This consists of memory data <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}=\{S_{0},\dots,S_{t-1}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}=\{S_{0},\dots,S_{t-1}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}=\{s_{t},o_{t},\tilde{o}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t-1}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}=\{s_{t},o_{t},\tilde{o}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t-1}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. This information is retrieved and comprehensively provided as context enabling the robot to dynamically and intelligently interact with its environment, uncover hidden objects, and resolve queries effectively.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The ZS-IP Policy <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\pi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\pi)</annotation></semantics></math> first decides the proper type of interaction.
It then utilises <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and memory <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to select a precise trajectory of motion, <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. The policy balances exploration and task objectives by guiding the robot to actions that maximise the likelihood of answering the query. We transform the actions from the camera frame <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> to the robot’s base frame <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>. The robot transitions between configurations <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> for movements like reach-to-grasp/push (using OMPL planner) whereas in pushing movements the robot follows a continuous trajectory (using Pilz Industrial Motion Planner).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Robot interaction</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We categorised robot actions to evaluate the contribution of each mode of interaction (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>) move camera-in-hand, (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) push, (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>) grasp (pick-and-place) and (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{4}</annotation></semantics></math>) lift to a stationary camera to investigate.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">(<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>) the robot simply moves the camera on its wrist to improve its view of the target object. The robot adjusts the orientation of its end-effector based on the object’s shape and orientation, enabling it to look into or beside the object to gain better visibility.
(<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) the robot performs pushing actions. <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> analyses the push line trajectories (added by enhanced observation) and selects the optimal push line for the task.
(<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{a}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{a}_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>) Grasping actions are guided by key points generated by enhanced observation. <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> selects the most feasible key point as the <span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grasp location</span>, indicating where the object should be grasped. Additionally, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> determines a <span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">place location</span>, representing the target position for placing the object after grasping.
(<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{4}</annotation></semantics></math>) The robot first executes the grasping action using the grasping key points, <em id="S3.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic"><math id="S3.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{G}</annotation></semantics></math></em>. It then positions the object in front of the secondary camera, which is fixed on the table (Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, top left). The robot holds the object until an image is captured, ensuring that it can accurately answer the query <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, e.g., <span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“What is written under the eraser?”</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">All the key points, push lines and 2-D grid, are mapped into the robot’s base frame. For improved precision, we use zoomed-in images for ZS-IP to select the key points or push lines.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering">Push lines</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S3.F2.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:155.3pt;">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4"><img src="2602.18374v1/Figures/rss25/overall_setup_.JPG" id="S3.F2.g5" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:103/69;" width="103" height="69" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4"><img src="2602.18374v1/Figures/rss25/task4_.JPG" id="S3.F2.g6" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:103/69;" width="103" height="69" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4"><img src="2602.18374v1/Figures/rss25/task5_keypoints_0.png" id="S3.F2.g7" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:103/72;" width="103" height="72" alt="Refer to caption"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_4"><img src="2602.18374v1/Figures/rss25/task5_keypoints_1.png" id="S3.F2.g8" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:103/75;" width="103" height="75" alt="Refer to caption"></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering">Grasp keypoints</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Four 2x2 images to the left show Push lines:</span>(Top left and right) A virtual 2D grid overlaid on the table, projected onto the 2D image, along with push lines generated for Task I (Query: What is under the eraser?). The robot selects P3 as the pre-contact point (bottom left) and D3 as the post-contact point (bottom right) to execute the pushing action. This interaction successfully uncovers and reveals the box of paper clips previously hidden underneath.
<span id="S3.F2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Four 2x2 images to the right show setup and Grasp keypoints:</span> Top: Robotic setup (left), scene for task VI; Bottom: key points generated for two objects in Task V involving pick-and-place at time step 1 (left) and 2 (right).
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Iterative Process:</span>
The robot starts in a home configuration, capturing an initial observation <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <span id="S3.SS4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Perception Analyser</span> evaluates observation and generates a response <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t},q)</annotation></semantics></math>. If a conclusive answer is not generated, <span id="S3.SS4.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Enhanced Observation</span> generates the corresponding annotated images and passes it to Action Block that generates action <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">x</mtext><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>o</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}=\pi(\mathcal{M}_{t},\textbf{x}_{t},z_{t},\tilde{o}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> using the <span id="S3.SS4.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Memory</span> state, <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, to generate an action <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, which changes the workspace and acquires a new observation <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>. The updated observation <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> is fed back into the Perception Analyser, <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t+1}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t+1},q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t+1}=\mathcal{F}_{VLM}({o}_{t+1},q)</annotation></semantics></math> continuing the iterative process until the query is resolved or the maximum iteration limit is reached.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">By combining interactive perception with semantic reasoning through VLMs, the proposed framework allows robots to manipulate their environments iteratively, revealing occluded information and improving task performance</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiment Setup and Structure</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Robotic Setup:</em>
The experiments were conducted using a 7-DOF Franka Emika Panda arm. The robot was equipped with an Intel RealSense RGB-D camera (Cam1) mounted on its end-effectors and another RGB camera (Cam2) mounted on the frame attached to the table (see Fig. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.4 Robot interaction ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> top left). The robot starts from the home configuration, and the RGB input taken from Cam1 is utilised to analyse spatial relationships, while depth information was leveraged to estimate the object’s distance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To enhance spatial localization and precise action execution, we placed an <em id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">ArUco marker</em> within the robot’s workspace. The marker served as an anchor for generating the 2D virtual grid. In future, we plan to remove the marker from our framework. The workspace included objects selected from the <em id="S4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">YCB</em> object set <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, ensuring diverse testing scenarios with varying levels of complexity and occlusion.
We integrated the GPT-4o model as the Perception Analyser to interpret visual inputs and guide the robot’s actions.
The VLM temperature parameter was set to zero to increase the consistency and reproducibility of results.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Experimental Design:</em>
To evaluate the ZS-IP framework, we designed experiments with varying task complexities and scenarios. The following aspects were analysed: (<em id="S4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">i</em>) Comparing interactive perception to baseline scenarios with static observations (i.e., passive perception).
(<em id="S4.p3.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">ii</em>) Evaluating different modes of workspace interaction, including camera-in-hand movement, pushing objects, grasping objects, and lifting objects for further investigation.
(<em id="S4.p3.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">iii</em>) Assessing the influence of enhanced observation, e.g., 2D grid-based augmented annotation, augmented key points, and pushing lines, on decision-making and performance.
(<em id="S4.p3.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">iv</em>) Measuring the framework’s adaptability to complex environments with partially or fully occluded objects.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We designed eight tasks with varying levels of complexity to test all four action categories.
The ZS-IP chooses suitable action categories across all tasks based on the contextual requirements of the scene. Each task was executed 10 times with slight variations in positioning and orientation of objects. Results are reported in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5 Results and Discussion ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The prompts and corresponding images are listed out in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Tasks in Designed Experiments ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a> while Fig. <a href="#A1.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ A.2 Additional Images ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows tasks I (top), II (middle) and III (bottom row).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Performance Metrics</em>:
We adopted and modified evaluation metrics inspired by the R2R-VLN dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>, tailoring them for our interactive manipulation tasks: <em id="S4.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Success Rate</em> (<span id="S4.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SR</span>): The percentage of trials in which the robot could correctly give a <em id="S4.p5.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">conclusive answer to the query</em>.
<em id="S4.p5.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Total Length (Position)</em> (<span id="S4.p5.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TL</span>): The mean total distance travelled by the robot across all trials. <em id="S4.p5.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Total Length (Position, Successful)</em> (<span id="S4.p5.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TLS</span>): The mean total distance travelled by the robot across successful trials.
<em id="S4.p5.1.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Position Error</em> (<span id="S4.p5.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PE</span>): The mean Euclidean distance between the robot’s final position and the target position.
<em id="S4.p5.1.11" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Oracle Success Rate</em> (<span id="S4.p5.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OSR</span>): The success rate when the robot stops at the closest point (within a margin of <math id="S4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1\&gt;m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo lspace="0.220em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1\&gt;m</annotation></semantics></math>) to the goal point annotated by a human.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We also compared ZS-IP with MOKA, which is a state-of-the-art motion generation framework for open-world robotic manipulation. MOKA uses point-based affordance representation to bridge the gap between VLM’s prediction on RGB images and robot’s motion  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>. For a fair comparison we adapt the output with Enhanced Observation (<math id="S4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO</annotation></semantics></math>) while retaining the functionality of the other components.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">This comprehensive experimental setup allows us to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed Interactive Perception framework in dynamically modifying the workspace and resolving queries involving partially or fully hidden objects.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Results and Discussion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Task Success Rates:</em> ZS-IP achieved high success rates on less complex tasks (Tasks I, II, and IV), demonstrating strong reasoning, perception, and memory-guided manipulation capabilities. In Task I, ZS-IP successfully planned and executed object interactions; in Task II, it autonomously altered lighting conditions by moving a tin to reveal a hidden object. In Task IV, it leveraged temporal memory to track a block’s position and expose hidden text beneath it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Task III was more challenging, requiring precise pushing to retrieve a pen drive buried under clutter. Failures stemmed from delicate manipulation demands and exceeding the five-iteration limit. Similarly, Task V involved placing two blocks in a box while preserving their spatial relationship—ZS-IP performed well (SR = 0.8), with failures due to errors in spatial reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Task VI required lifting an eraser to read its surface text. ZS-IP used a secondary camera effectively, achieving a success rate of 0.8. Across tasks, the system showed resilience to positional and orientational variance, validating its generalisation to unstructured scenes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Notably, performance in more complex tasks (e.g., Task III and Task VII) highlighted the framework’s reasoning, memory recall, and precise sequencing of combined actions. These results showcase its robustness and potential for adaptation to more complex scenes in unstructured environments.
We also observed that ZS-IP demonstrated robustness to variations in object position and orientation, successfully completing tasks despite changes in spatial configuration.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>ZS-IP performed for eight different tasks with different required levels of complexity from easy (i.e. Task I) to more complex (Task VIII) interactions. Four categories of interaction are considered: ‘Pushing’, ‘Pick-and-place’ or ‘Grasping’, ‘Lifting’ an object to investigate it, and ‘observe’. Each task is performed 10 times, and the results show the success rate out of 10 trials. </figcaption>

</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Tasks VII and VIII, representing the highest levels of complexity, were assessed across all five frameworks. Oracle positions for these tasks were determined through human-annotated ground truth labelling, performed post-experimentation for each scene. Each scene incorporated a single predefined push line and a designated key point, both manually specified by an expert annotator. These annotations were carefully selected to minimise scene disruption while ensuring successful task execution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For the <em id="S5.p6.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">ZS-IP In-Context</em>, two annotated images and corresponding instructions were provided before the system was exposed to the query of the current task. This approach aimed to enhance contextual understanding and action selection, improving performance in these more demanding scenarios. To aid semantic understanding of the scene, we introduce a Retrieval Augmented In-context Generation (RAIG) method, explained in the Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Retrieval Augmented In-context Generation (RAIG) ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>, but is opted out during experimentation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.p7.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Task VII Analysis:</em> ZS-IP Push failed to resolve <em id="S5.p7.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Task VII</em> (Fig. <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ A.2 Additional Images ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> a-c) as the bottom face of the eraser remained occluded, requiring lifting and reorientation for visibility by Cam2. Despite multiple pushing attempts, ZS-IP lacked sufficient task knowledge and returned ‘None’, indicating no viable action. This likely stemmed from VLM hallucination, as it prematurely assumed the eraser text was in English without evidence. While ZS-IP Grasp could theoretically solve the task by relocating surrounding objects, it failed after exceeding the five-iteration limit.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p8.1" class="ltx_p">The MOKA framework, despite using both pushing and grasping actions alongside in-context examples, also failed to complete the task. Pushing an object proved to be a challenge for MOKA as the VLM was unable to suggest pre- and post-contact points only based on the discrete 2D grid. It was also limited by the lack of memory retention for prior states and scene configurations. An ablation was performed by comparing PIVOT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite> (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS4" title="A.4 Ablation studies ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.4</span></a>) on one task each from the ‘grasping’, ‘lifting’, and ‘Observe’ categories and found that ZS-IP has higher SR. We also compare against varying VLMs outside and within OpenAI’s GPT and find GPT-4 to have the highest SR.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison of methods and failure analysis: </span>
To rigorously evaluate the limits of our framework, we conducted an in-depth analysis of more complex scenarios for Task VII and VIII (presented in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5 Results and Discussion ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Task VII is similar to Task VI but has additional complexity imposed by obstructing objects on both sides of the eraser. This necessitates multi-step reasoning, requiring ZS-IP to push and separate the obstructing objects before grasping eraser. This process involved <em id="S5.p9.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">sequential decision-making by retrieving past data from memory</em>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Comparing ZS-IP with different features and MOKA. <td id="S5.T2.2.1.8.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_b ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T2.2.1.8.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5</span></td></tr>
