</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ZS-IP In-Context</span> demonstrated a significantly higher SR of 0.7, benefiting from its ability to delay the grasping action until the eraser was entirely free from obstructions. Notably, the Total Length (TL) for <span id="S5.p10.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ZS-IP In-Context</span> was higher compared to ZS-IP due to the VLM occasionally recommending the removal of all surrounding obstacles—including the red container and the Lego structure—before attempting a grasp. While this approach deviated from the oracle manipulation strategy, which prioritised direct manipulation of the eraser, it ensured grasping under optimal conditions, thereby reducing execution errors and increasing overall success.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S5.p11.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Task VIII Analysis:</em>
Task VIII (Fig. <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ A.2 Additional Images ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>d) involved locating a strawberry inside a cup. However, to introduce additional complexity, a brown book was placed at an incline, partially obstructing the robot’s direct line of sight. While all methods, except grasping, managed to handle this scenario, the task required ZS-IP to conduct precise scene analysis to guide the in-hand camera over the target object for visibility. Additionally, within the pushing action category, ZS-IP had to predict and execute a carefully controlled sideways push near the centre to prevent unnecessary disruptions and further complications.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p12.1" class="ltx_p">ZS-IP Observe demonstrated notable efficiency in navigating toward the cup, reducing TL, TLS, and PE. However, it successfully identified the strawberry inside the cup only once. Although ZS-IP accurately provided end-effector targets based on <math id="S5.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{ap}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{ap}</annotation></semantics></math> to position the robot near the cup, it failed to correctly classify the red object as a strawberry in six instances. This failure resulted from the shadow cast by the inclined book, which obstructed essential visual cues for reliable object recognition. Even after repositioning the robot closer to the cup, ZS-IP Observe lacked sufficient contextual understanding to effectively disambiguate the occluded scene.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p13.1" class="ltx_p">While Task VIII did not heavily rely on memory capabilities, the baseline MOKA method achieved an SR of only 0.5, primarily due to its dependence on a fixed 2D grid. Selecting a grid location near the top or bottom of the book often led to misaligned pre-contact and post-contact points. Consequently, the robot frequently pushed either the cup or the book’s base, causing unintended scene disruptions such as the cup toppling over. These results underscore the limitations of rigid 2D-based approaches in tasks that require precise and adaptive interactions and highlight the advantage of the closed-loop perception-action framework of ZS-IP, as well as the impact of push lines in complex and unstructured environments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced ZS-IP, an interactive perception framework that integrates VLMs with robotic systems for dynamic scene exploration. By leveraging semantic segmentation, 2D spatial grids, grasping key points, and push-line annotations, ZS-IP enables robots to iteratively gather visual information and infer the presence of partially or fully occluded objects.
Our experiments with a 7-DOF robotic arm demonstrated the efficiency of ZS-IP in highly challenging scenarios, where goal objects were entirely hidden and required multi-step reasoning combined with efficient memory retrieval. The comparative analysis with baseline methods, such as MOKA, highlights the superiority of ZS-IP, underscoring the importance of memory retrieval and dynamic observation gathering.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Despite the advantages of ZS-IP, its performance is constrained by several factors. One notable limitation is the low-resolution depth information, which restricts precise interaction with objects, particularly in cluttered environments where fine-grained manipulation is required. Additionally, integrating large models in real-time for multi-modal reasoning remains an open challenge and a promising avenue for future research.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Future work will focus on extending ZS-IP to more realistic, real-world scenarios beyond controlled laboratory settings. A key application area is agricultural robotics, where tasks such as fruit picking demand the ability to identify and differentiate ripe fruits hidden behind leaves while avoiding unripe ones. Another significant challenge lies in enhancing the common-sense reasoning capabilities of VLMs. For instance, in the task of arranging two wooden blocks next to each other inside a cardboard box, the VLM sometimes incorrectly stacks one block on top of another and classifies the task as <span id="S7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">successful</span>, as observed in the supplementary video. However, from a human perspective, such cases represent failure modes, as documented in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5 Results and Discussion ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, Task V. This discrepancy between VLM-driven task evaluation and human common sense highlights the need for improved reasoning mechanisms in VLMs in robotics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, ZS-IP’s current manipulation capabilities remain constrained in terms of action representation. At present, grasping is performed using rotation in <math id="S7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SO(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">SO(2)</annotation></semantics></math> and translation in <math id="S7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, while pushing actions are limited to translations in <math id="S7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. These constraints restrict the system’s ability to manipulate objects in more complex environments where full <math id="S7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SE(3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">SE(3)</annotation></semantics></math> transformations are required. Future work will focus on extending ZS-IP’s pushing and grasping capabilities to enable more adaptive and robust interactions in unstructured settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, incorporating additional sensing modalities, such as tactile feedback and proprioceptive sensing, holds great potential for enhancing ZS-IP’s capabilities in physical interaction. These modalities would enable richer environmental feedback, allowing for more precise and dexterous manipulation. By addressing these limitations, we aim to further advance ZS-IP towards real-world deployment in diverse, challenging environments.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Appendix</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Retrieval Augmented In-context Generation (RAIG)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Once the output from Perception Analyser is obtained, we move to the augmenting the semantic understanding of the scene using this module.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We utilize <span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Retrieval-Augmented In-Context Generation</span> (RAIG) with eight in-context examples sourced from the Visual Reasoning task suite of the VIMA Benchmark dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, focusing specifically on enhancing the visual perception capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs).</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In-context data generation:</span>
We re-implement the Visual Reasoning tasks internally using a demonstrator that chooses from five atomic functions: <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">reach_object()</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pick_up()</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">go_to()</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">place()</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">push()</span>. For each execution, we record the end-effector positions and corresponding image frames upon function completion. The collected data is temporally ordered and processed to serve as input to a VLM. The VLM then generates structured outputs, including a query description, a detailed task description, the inferred action type (e.g., <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">push</span> or <span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grasp</span>), and a rationale for the chosen action.
All tasks are executed using an impedance-controlled Franka Emika Panda robot, configured with zero-torque and gravity compensation enabled to ensure safe and compliant interaction. This setup is intended to produce high-quality data that supports reproducibility, improves future context generation, and leverages the expected continual improvements in large vision-language models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Context Retrieval:</span>
Following the methodology outlined in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, we compute embeddings of the VLM-generated outputs from the Perception Analyser and each in-context example. Cosine similarity is used to retrieve the top-<math id="A1.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> most similar examples. We use SentenceBERT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> to compute embeddings, enabling semantically meaningful comparisons across textual contexts.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Action generation:</span>
The retrieved <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> in-context examples are then fed into the VLM. Based on its interpretation of the current image frame and commonsense reasoning, the VLM selects both the target object and the most relevant example. The action type associated with the selected in-context example is then executed.
This VLM-driven selection dictates both <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">what</span> action is performed and <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">on which</span> object. Notably, naively executing the top-ranked retrieved example, without further VLM inference, often resulted in incorrect behavior, such as performing a <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grasp</span> instead of a <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">place</span>. Moreover, presenting all <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> examples simultaneously, as done in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, led to a consistent defaulting to the <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grasp</span> action type. We attribute this to the underrepresentation of <span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">pushing</span> actions in VLM training datasets, which are predominantly composed of pick-and-place interactions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Task VII being successfully performed at various time steps (query: ‘What language is the text written in on the black eraser?’): (a) <math id="A1.F4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math>: {<math id="A1.F4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1},o_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1},o_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>} with pushing action proposed, <math id="A1.F4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{P}</annotation></semantics></math>, (b) <math id="A1.F4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=2</annotation></semantics></math>: {<math id="A1.F4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2},o_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2},o_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>} after pushing, red and yellow objects are separated from the eraser. Grasping key points are now proposed <math id="A1.F4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="EO_{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">EO_{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, (c) <math id="A1.F4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=2</annotation></semantics></math>: Cam2 view of eraser that is lifted and moved by the robot in front of the Cam2, (d) Task VIII: brown book partially occludes the view into the cup.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>(From left to right) First and Third row: Task I to VIII. Second and Fourth row: the robot’s workspace in Task I to VIII. Task I: the robot needs to push the eraser to see the box of paper clips underneath. Task II: The robot needs to pick up the aluminium tin and place it elsewhere to see the screw in the shadow. Task III: Push the Lego blocks to see the pen-drive underneath. Task IV: Pick up the blue block and place it elsewhere to see the text written on the paper under it. Task V: Identify the red block and green Lego structure on the table. Arrange them inside the cardboard box while maintaining their original spatial positions relative to one another. Task VI: grasp the black eraser and bring it in front of the secondary camera to see what is written on the side under it. Task VII: similar to Task VI but eraser is between two objects. Hence ZS-IP requires first pushing the eraser and then grasping to complete the task. Task VIII: ZS-IP should see what is inside the cup covered by the brown book. </figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A1.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ A.3 Tasks in Designed Experiments ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> presents the tasks used in the ZS-IP evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task I:</span> The robot pushes the eraser to reveal the box of paper clips beneath it.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task II:</span> The robot picks up the aluminium tin and relocates it to expose the screw hidden in the shadow.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task III:</span> The robot pushes the Lego blocks to uncover the pen drive underneath.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task IV:</span> The robot picks up the blue block and moves it to reveal the text written on the paper beneath it.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task V:</span> The robot identifies the red block and green Lego structure on the table, arranging them inside the cardboard box while preserving their original spatial relationships.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task VI:</span> The robot grasps the black eraser and brings it in front of the secondary camera to examine the text written on its underside.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task VII:</span> Similar to Task VI, but with the eraser positioned between two objects, requiring ZS-IP to first push the eraser before grasping it to complete the task.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task VIII:</span> The robot determines the contents of a cup covered by a brown book.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>

<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Ablation studies</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A1.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ A.4 Ablation studies ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows that ZS-IP outperforms PIVOT with and without interactive perception. This is attributed to the improvement in VLM visual reasoning capability induced by the Enhanced Observation (EO).</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#A1.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ A.4 Ablation studies ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5 Results and Discussion ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> compare the performance of GPT-4o with other VLMs and varying VLM version within GPT. We only compare for one task each from ”grasping”, ”lifting”, and ”observe” to gain an understanding of the output and reasoning capabilites of the various models.</p>
</div>

<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Prompts</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Perception Analyser processes the scene and generates an output guiding ZS-IP to the next step. Appendix Figure <a href="#A1.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ A.5 Prompts ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> illustrates the base prompt. In the first iteration, the Perception Analyser operates without memory, while from the second iteration onward, memory is introduced in the form of prior actions, thoughts, and images. The template is presented in Appendix Figure <a href="#A1.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ A.5 Prompts ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, and an example output is shown in Appendix Figure <a href="#A1.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ A.5 Prompts ‣ Appendix A Appendix ‣ Zero-shot Interactive Perception" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F6" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.F6.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="461.27" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 461.27" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,461.27) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#404040;" fill="#404040" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 455.37 C 0 458.63 2.64 461.27 5.91 461.27 L 544.09 461.27 C 547.36 461.27 550 458.63 550 455.37 L 550 5.91 C 550 2.64 547.36 0 544.09 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2F2;" fill="#F2F2F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 437.16 L 548.03 437.16 L 548.03 5.91 C 548.03 3.73 546.27 1.97 544.09 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 445.76)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.62em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="506.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Perception Analyser</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 17.24)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.62em;--ltx-fo-height:29.49em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="411.58" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 408.12)" width="506.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are an intelligent embodied agent that can thoroughly perform object detection and action planning. Your job is to analyse the provided image and precisely answer the input task or text question, selecting and justifying an appropriate action if required. The image is captured by a camera mounted on a Franka Panda robotic manipulator.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Instructions:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Understand the Question:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Identify the Goal Object mentioned or implied in the question.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- If no Goal Object is specified, focus on the general intent of the question.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Analyze the Image:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Detect and list all visible objects in the image.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Determine if the Goal Object is fully visible, partially obscured, or completely hidden.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Take Action:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- If the Goal Object is obscured:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Identify the object obstructing it the most (the Target Object).</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Analyse the scene, focusing on the key details relevant to answering the question. Think about one action or series of actions that need to be taken to complete the task</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- If the Goal Object is visible:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Answer the question based on its attributes or position.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">4. Decision:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- State if you have conclusively completed the task in question now (Yes/No).</span></span>
<span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F6.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- While some tasks can be completed using only one action, others may require a sequence (e.g., ”push” followed by ”grasp”).</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Perception Analyser</figcaption>
</figure>

<span id="A1.F9.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Prompt provided to VLM to suggest grasp Keypoints</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.47)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.62em;--ltx-fo-height:67.9em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="942.16" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 939.47)" width="506.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are an intelligent embodied agent that can perform interactive perception using visual and textual information. Your job is to analyse the provided image of a tabletop scene and suggest actions based on an input text question and task. The image is captured by a camera mounted on the wrist of Franka Panda robotic manipulator.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Your goal is to suggest keypoints for the robotic arm to grasp the target object, with the ultimate aim of gaining more visual information to complete the input task or answer the input question.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Inputs Provided:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. **Current Time Step**:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **RGB Image**: A visual representation of the tabletop scene.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **2D Grid Cube Image**: An image with a 5x5 grid overlay, annotated with x and y coordinates in the format [x; y]. This grid serves as the coordinate system for robotic arm actions.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Keypoints Image**: An RGB image with Keypoints overlay. The keypoints are annotated with letters ”P” followed by a number</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Optional RGB Image**: A visual representation of the bottom surface of the grasped object may be provided</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. **Historical Data**:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- RGB images of the scene from all previous time steps, with the most recent towards the end.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Outputs from the previous time step:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Previous Action**: The action you suggested to perform the task.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Previous Scene Analysis**: Reasoning about the scene, including occlusions of the target object.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Previous Place Location**: The grid coordinate where the target object was placed.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Previous Contact Location**: The keypoint suggested for grasping the target object.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### 2D Grid coordinate system:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- The grid’s x and y coordinates represent positions within the 2D cube coordinate frame.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Base of table: Lower limit of 2D cube’s x-axis i.e (0,0 to 5,0)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Top of table: Upper limit of 2D cube’s x-axis i.e (0,5 to 5,5)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Left of table: Upper limit of 2D cube’s y-axis i.e (0,0 to 0,5)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.21.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Right of table: Lower limit of 2D cube’s y-axis i.e (5,0 to 5,5)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.22" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.22.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Task Objective:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.23" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.23.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Analyse the provided visual and textual data to:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.24" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.24.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. Determine the best keypoint on the target object for the robotic arm to perform grasping. Choose only from keypoints **on the Target Object** you want to move.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.25" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.25.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Determine the best grid location for placing the target object.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.26" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.26.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Minimize disturbances to the scene while achieving the desired task outcome.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.27" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.27.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Key Instructions:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.28" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.28.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- output: You must suggest the best place location</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.29" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.29.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Perform chain-of-thought reasoning</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.30" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.30.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Note that vertex_x and vertex_y are continuous float values rounded to one decimal place in the 2D cube coordinate frame</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.31" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.31.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Special Case for Time Step 0:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.32" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.32.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- If the current time step is ‘0‘, it indicates the first iteration of the task.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.33" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.33.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- All previous outputs (Scene Analysis, Action, Place Location, and Contact Keypoint) will be empty.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.34" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F9.pic1.2.34.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- **Important**: The information from previous time steps indicates that the robotic task was complete, incomplete, or only partially successful. Use the provided textual and image data to generate an improved and complete solution for the task. Focus on precision, efficiency, and achieving the desired outcome.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span>Prompt for grasping</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A1.F10" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.F10.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="676.44" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 676.44" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,676.44) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#404040;" fill="#404040" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 670.53 C 0 673.8 2.64 676.44 5.91 676.44 L 544.09 676.44 C 547.36 676.44 550 673.8 550 670.53 L 550 5.91 C 550 2.64 547.36 0 544.09 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2F2;" fill="#F2F2F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 652.33 L 548.03 652.33 L 548.03 5.91 C 548.03 3.73 546.27 1.97 544.09 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 660.93)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.62em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="506.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Prompt provided to VLM for ZS-IP observe</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.55)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.62em;--ltx-fo-height:45.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:10pt;" height="626.75" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 623.98)" width="506.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.62em;">
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are an intelligent embodied agent that can perfrom active perception using visual and textual information. Your job is to analyse the provided image of a tabletop scene based on an input task and text question. The image is captured by a camera mounted on the wrist of Franka Panda robotic manipulator.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Your goal is to suggest camera positions and orientations for the robotic arm to find the target object, with the ultimate aim of gaining more visual information to complete the input task or answer the input question.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The input image will have a 3D cube with 3x3 grids overlaid on it. the grid’s x and y vertices will be annotated in the format [x; y]. You must use the below conventions while proving the output</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Base of table: Lower limit of 3D cube’s x-axis i.e (0,0 to 5,0)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Top of table: Upper limit of 3D cube’s x-axis i.e (0,5 to 5,5)</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Layer Mapping: The 3D cube’s z-axis consists of 3 discrete layers that are color coded. They represent the depth.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_z = 0 (Blue layer) is at the table surface.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_z = 1 (Black layer) is 10 cm above the table .</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_z = 2 (Green layer) is the topmost layer, 20 cm above the table.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Orientation Mapping: This is the fixed orientation of 35 degrees about x-axis (roll in our case).</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- orient_x = 0 when the target object of interest is flat on the table and perpendicular to the table</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- orient_x = 1 for a +35° roll. Target is inclined towards the Base of Table</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- orient_x = 2 for a -35° roll. Target is inclined towards the Top of Table</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You take actions by suggesting new camera positions and orientations with respect to 3D cube coordinate frame. The camera has an offset only along the z-axis and stops 35 cm above a given vertex_z. You can suggest new meaningful camera positions and orientations to gain more visual information with the ultimate goal of being able to answer the input text question.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">At each step you will be given your ”State History” i.e position and orientation in the 3D cube’s coordinate frame. You are encouraged to explore the environment while avoiding revisiting states by comparing with ”State History”.</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Action Output consists of the next best camera location:</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_x: Positive continuous value along x-axis in the cube coordinate frame rounded to one decimal</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_y: Positive continuous value along y-axis in the cube coordinate frame rounded to one decimal</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- vertex_z: Integer value along z-axis based on the Layer Mapping</span></span>
<span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.F10.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- orient_x: Integer value based on Orientation Mapping</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span>Prompt to perform camera in-hand movement</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
